entries.quote: Note that the card number is not editable once saved

entries.title: FD150: where the customer enters a PIN
steps: The customer can enter the PIN on the FD150 itself.
If an RP10 PIN pad is attached, the customer can enter it there instead.
entries.quote: Yes, the customer can enter their PIN on the FD150 itself or via

entries.title: FD150: the RP10 PIN pad is optional
steps: The FD150 works on its own.
It can run credit and debit transactions without a PIN pad.
entries.quote: No. You can use the FD150 terminal independently and run credit

entries.title: FD150: tap payments and mobile wallets are accepted
steps: The FD150 can take NFC payments such as Apple Pay and Samsung Pay, other mobile wallets and contactless cards.
entries.quote: Yes. It can accept NFC payments like Apple PayTM, Samsung Pay, and

entries.title: FD150: EBT is accepted
steps: The FD150 accepts electronic benefits transfer (EBT) transactions.
entries.quote: Yes. The FD150 accepts electronic benefits transfer (EBT)

entries.title: FD150: more than one merchant account on one terminal
steps: The FD150 supports multi-merchant processing, so one terminal can process for more than one merchant account.
Contact us to have this set up.
entries.quote: more than one merchant account using a single terminal

entries.title: FD150: ways it can connect
steps: The FD150 connects to the network over IP (Ethernet), dial-up or Wi-Fi.
It has three USB ports.
entries.quote: Uses IP, dial-up, or Wi-Fi to connect to the network.

entries.title: FD150: run a sale (chip, tap or swipe)
steps: Touch Sale.
Key in the amount and press Enter.
If tips are enabled, key in the tip amount and press Enter, or press Cancel to skip.
Swipe, tap or insert the card.
If the terminal asks after a swipe, select Credit or Debit.
If asked, enter the Clerk/Server number and press Enter.
If asked for a PIN, have the customer enter it, or leave it blank and press Enter to bypass.
With a chip card, remove the card when the terminal prompts.
Wait while the terminal gets an approval code.
Choose whether to print a customer copy: touch No or Yes.
The terminal returns to the main screen by itself.
entries.quote: Swipe, Tap, or Insert the card into the terminal

entries.title: FD150: PIN bypass does not work on tap payments
steps: On a swiped or inserted card the PIN can be left blank and Enter pressed to bypass it.
PIN bypass is not allowed on a contactless (tap) payment.
entries.quote: Note: PIN Bypass is not allowed on contactless

entries.title: FD150: prompt to remove the chip card before it connects
steps: This is normal on a chip transaction.
Remove the card when prompted; the terminal then connects to the host for approval.
entries.quote: Note: If chip entry then the terminal will prompt to remove the card before it connects out to the host

entries.title: FD150: refund a card
steps: Touch Other.
Touch Refund.
Key in the amount and press Enter.
Swipe, tap or insert the card, or type the card number and press Enter.
If the terminal asks after a swipe, select Credit.
If asked, enter the Clerk/Server number and press Enter.
With a chip card, remove the card when the terminal prompts.
Wait while the terminal gets an approval code.
Choose whether to print a customer copy: touch No or Yes.
The terminal returns to the main screen by itself.
entries.quote: Swipe, Tap, or Insert the card into the terminal or type in the card number and press Enter

entries.title: FD150 (restaurant): open a tab
steps: Touch Other.
Touch More.
Touch Tabs.
Touch Open.
Enter the tab amount and press Enter.
Swipe, tap or insert the card, or type the card number.
If asked after a swipe, touch Credit.
If asked, enter the SERVER number and press Enter.
If asked for a PIN, enter it or leave it blank and press Enter.
Wait while the terminal gets an approval code.
Choose whether to print a customer copy: touch No or Yes.
The terminal goes back to the main screen.
entries.quote: Enter desired Tab amount and press Enter

entries.title: FD150: an open tab must be closed to get paid
steps: Opening a tab does not capture the funds.
Do a Close Tab to capture them.
entries.quote: Note: A Close Tab function will need to be performed to capture funds.

entries.title: FD150: check a gift card balance
steps: Touch Other.
Touch Gift Card.
Touch Balance Inquiry.
Swipe the card, or key in the card number and press Enter.
The terminal connects out and prints a receipt with the balance.
The terminal returns to the main screen by itself.
entries.quote: The terminal will communicate out to verify and print a receipt with the balance

entries.title: Datawire Error 1007 (also shown as VXN Error 52/53)
steps: The terminal cannot communicate with the host.
Check that the date and time on the main screen are correct.
If they are, make sure you have a stable internet connection.
Power the terminal off, unplug the Ethernet cable for about 30 seconds, plug it back in, then power the terminal on.
If the error still appears, try a different Ethernet cable or another port on your router.
entries.quote: Datawire Error 1007 (also shown as VXN Error 52/53) indicates that your terminal is unable to communicate with the host.
entries.note: Tier 2 (Paysafe). The page gives typical causes as incorrect terminal settings, outdated applications or network connectivity issues.

entries.title: First Data terminal: settle the batch by hand (Paysafe)
steps: Go to the terminal's main screen.
Select Close or Close Batch, depending on the model.
Confirm by selecting OK on the touch screen.
entries.quote: Depending on your model, select “Close” or “Close Batch.”
entries.note: Tier 2. Fiserv's own FD 130/150 steps reach Close Batch through the Other button.

entries.title: FD150: delete a batch (Paysafe)
steps: From the idle screen tap the orange tools icon.
Select Settings.
Tap Credit, then choose Delete Batch.
Enter the password and press the green key.
When the terminal asks "Delete Pre-Auth Batch", select No.
Press the red key 3 times to return to the idle screen.
entries.quote: Tap on Credit and then choose Delete Batch
entries.note: Tier 2. Possible default passwords listed: 990712; 766130; 123123; 123456. The page says this step might also require an FD-generated daily password.

entries.title: FD150 prompt: "Delete Pre-Auth Batch"
steps: This prompt appears after a batch has been deleted.
Select No.
entries.quote: After the batch is deleted, the terminal will prompt “Delete Pre‑Auth Batch”, select No
entries.note: Tier 2 (Paysafe).

entries.title: FD150: change the date and time (Paysafe)
steps: From the idle screen tap the orange tools icon.
Select Date/Time.
Enter the date as MMDDYYYY and press the green key.
Enter the time in military format (HHMMSS) and press the green key again.
Press the red key once to return to the idle screen.
entries.quote: Enter the time in military format (HHMMSS) and press the green key again
entries.note: Tier 2.

entries.title: FD150: run a ping test to check the internet connection (Paysafe)
steps: From the idle screen tap the orange tools icon.
Select Lan and then Ping.
For the IP address, type www.yahoo.com and press the green key.
A successful test shows four responses with a time in ms.
Press the red key three times to return to the main screen.
entries.quote: If the test is successful, the terminal will show four responses with XXms
entries.note: Tier 2. Our sheet describes running Ping from the Wi-Fi settings; this page uses the Lan menu.

entries.title: FD150 ping test shows "NONE"
steps: The ping test failed: the terminal is not reaching the internet.
Check the network cable and your internet connection, then run the test again.
entries.quote: If the test fails, the terminal will display “NONE” instead of XXms
entries.note: Tier 2. The page only says NONE means the test failed; checking the cable and connection comes from the same publisher's Datawire 1007 page.

entries.title: FD150: connect to Wi-Fi (Paysafe)
steps: From the idle screen, tap the orange tools icon.
Select Wi-Fi, then choose Security.
Enter the security password and press the green key.
In the Security field, select the correct security level for the network.
Enter the Wi-Fi password in the Key field.
Enter the network name (SSID) and press the green key.
Confirm the changes by selecting Yes.
The terminal reboots to apply the settings.
entries.quote: In the Security field, select the correct security level for the network
entries.note: Tier 2. The page does not say what the "security password" is.

entries.title: FD150: Wi-Fi name or password has characters the keypad cannot type (Paysafe)
steps: Connect a USB keyboard to the terminal and type them on that.
To switch between lowercase and uppercase on the terminal, press and hold the green key and then press the ALPHA key; repeat to switch back.
entries.quote: To switch between lowercase and uppercase letters, press and hold the green key, then press the ALPHA key.
entries.note: Tier 2.

entries.title: FD150: test the keypad when keys do not respond (Paysafe)
steps: From the idle screen, tap the orange tools icon.
Select Diagnostics and then Keypad.
Press different keys on the terminal to test them.
Press the red key three times to return to the main screen.
entries.quote: Select Diagnostics and then Keypad
entries.note: Tier 2.

entries.title: FD150: find the terminal's device ID (Paysafe)
steps: From the idle screen, tap the orange tools icon.
Select Settings and then Credit.
Tap Parameters.
Select View Parms.
Enter the password and press the green key.
Tap Host and select Next.
The screen shows the device ID.
entries.quote: Tap Host and select Next
entries.note: Tier 2. Possible default passwords listed: 990712; 766130; 123123; 123456.
